nodes.label: Text-to-Lottie Skill/Harness
nodes.rationale: Open-source harness for generating production-ready Lottie animations via coding agents (claude code/codex). Prompt design intent: ground the model with concrete assets (SVGs, real-world data, screenshots) for better results; use motion-design terminology (ease-in/out); simulate camera moves (pushes, pans, zooms) through group transforms; expose only the controls the user requests (default output only exposes a background color control); and specify FPS/duration explicitly.

nodes.label: Fractional Positioning (MIN_SPACING = 1e-9)
nodes.rationale: Float positions (midpoint insertion) avoid renumbering on every move; MIN_SPACING = 1e-9 triggers a rebalance — never use integer positions.

nodes.label: Fractional Positions (MIN_SPACING = 1e-9)
nodes.rationale: Cards and columns use float positions (midpoint insertion); if spacing falls below MIN_SPACING = 1e-9 a rebalance is triggered.

nodes.label: Real-Time Degradation (Redis → SSE → in-process)
nodes.rationale: Redis Pub/Sub → SSE; gracefully degrades to in-process fan-out if Redis is unreachable (not an error state).

nodes.label: Real-Time Updates (Redis Pub/Sub → SSE)
nodes.rationale: Mutations publish to Redis Pub/Sub which fans out to clients over SSE; if Redis is down the app degrades to in-process fan-out (single server instance only, no presence).

nodes.label: Workspace Selection & Switching
nodes.rationale: Workspace selection persisted via localStorage; workspace switching enforces limits; settings form validation rules.

nodes.label: Dense Row List Page
nodes.rationale: The Board failure is card height (~110px rows, 29 cards = ~3200px scroll), not row count; a 40px dense Linear-style row is the actual win. ListView.tsx and boardViewUtils.ts are harvestable dense-row primitives from the rejected List/Calendar cycle.

nodes.label: Tracker Events
nodes.rationale: Separate activity system (tracker_events + recordTrackerActivity) instead of reusing card_events / recordActivity, accepted because Tracker history only surfaces on Tracker pages and card_events has a closed eventType union.

nodes.label: Tracker Items Entity
nodes.rationale: New table independent of cards (no FK) so weeks-horizon product/backlog work gets a durable record and stable citation key without retrofitting the global SERIAL cards.id or touching Board. Granularity is 1:N (one item spawns several Board cards), so write-back rules are unspecifiable.

nodes.label: Tracker Vocabularies
nodes.rationale: One vocabulary table with a kind discriminator (status/priority/label) chosen over three tables and over settings JSONB: three tables duplicate CRUD/seed patterns without benefit at dozens scale, and JSONB violates the typed-columns settings pattern. Fractional position supports ordered kinds.

nodes.label: Tracker Phases
nodes.rationale: Phase gets its own table rather than tracker_vocabularies.kind=phase because it needs subtitle, rename, delete and a project FK — all forbidden by vocabulary v1 rules.

nodes.label: Direction B (Status-Grouped Tracker Page)
nodes.rationale: Recommended: always status-grouped dense list with search only. Delivers the reference look for a fraction of Direction C's cost and defers axis-switching and filter-persistence decisions that cannot be answered honestly until real items exist. Cannot repeat the previous cycle's failure by construction because the data is new.

nodes.label: Done-Column Tower Problem
nodes.rationale: Spike found 29 cards in one Done column (~110px each) is the only pain with hard evidence; the cheaper fix is archive/collapse/filter Done on the Board, kept as a separate candidate so it is passed over deliberately, not silently ignored.

nodes.label: Direction A (Implicit Default Project)
nodes.rationale: Recommended in the pitch: auto-create a default project so /tracker stays a single route and existing items land in it; no URL segment can collide with the FA-1 key pattern. Later superseded by the spec, which ships a B/C hybrid because the user rejected a default project outright.

nodes.label: Additive Idempotent Migration
nodes.rationale: schema.sql re-runs in full on every make db-migrate with no migration-tracking table, so every backfill must carry a WHERE ... IS NULL guard; an unguarded position backfill would wipe every manual drag order on each deploy, and the category backfill must be appended after the retroactive seed block or fresh databases end up with NULL categories.

nodes.label: Client-Derived Rollup Design Decision
nodes.rationale: Option B chosen over server-computed aggregates (Option A) and hybrid (Option C): A does not deliver the payload saving because search-into-projects needs in-project items on the home payload anyway and makes live rollup expensive (separate invalidation path); C creates two rollup implementations that must agree forever (card says 63%, page says 61%, no way to tell which is right).

nodes.label: Derived Rollup Progress
nodes.rationale: Progress is fully derivable from item statuses; storing it creates a second source of truth. Client-derived over the existing full item list keeps one derivation path and one cache; server aggregates would need a separate invalidation path and a second rollup implementation that must agree forever.

nodes.label: Stable FA-N Keys
nodes.rationale: FA-N keys are stable citations already circulating in chat/DM; re-keying breaks live references, so allocation stays on workspaces.tracker_key_counter and keys remain workspace-scoped.

nodes.label: Manual Task Ordering (fractional position)
nodes.rationale: Fractional position scoped per (project_id, phase_id) bucket reuses position.ts. A reorder-only write must not bump version, while an assignment write must, or optimistic locking silently becomes version tracks some fields; a release caused by a project/phase delete bumps neither.

nodes.label: Overdue Signalling
nodes.rationale: Showing progress without overdue signalling makes the tracker actively lie (100% green while every date has passed). Requires end_date plus unfinished work; visual only, never blocking.

nodes.label: Status Category Semantics
nodes.rationale: Status vocabulary must carry machine-readable semantics (backlog/started/completed/canceled) because rollup percentage and overdue colouring both depend on it; name-regex inference (CANCELLED=/cancel/i) already renders a status named Selesai wrong. The vocabulary is closed to the five seeded rows, which makes provisioning on workspace creation mandatory.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Provisioning on Workspace Creation
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary was never provisioned at workspace creation (all three creation paths insert only the workspace and membership), so workspaces born after the last migrate have zero statuses and getBacklogStatusId throws. Closing the status vocabulary removes the last runtime fix, so seeding inside the creation transaction is in-scope and deliberate.

nodes.label: Camel Draw-On Lottie Animation Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Strokes trace the camel SVG contours with an animated trim path (draw-on effect), then a fill fades in once the lines are mostly drawn, then everything fades out for a seamless loop. Colors and line width are exposed as slotted controls (strokeColor, fillColor, strokeWidth, bgColor) per the text-to-lottie skill requirement; SVG text attribution is dropped on purpose; the script is build-time only and is not shipped in lottie.json.

nodes.rationale: Pre-existing card activity logger in server/src/routes/helpers.ts (lines 369-398) — referenced as the pattern to NOT extend and to NOT call for tracker mutations.

nodes.label: recordTrackerActivity
nodes.rationale: Helper in server/src/routes/tracker-activity.ts that inserts tracker_events rows (event_type + JSONB payload + actor + workspace_id). Kept separate from recordActivity() with a closed eventType union so tracker mutations never write to card_events.

nodes.label: Tracker DB Schema
nodes.rationale: Foundation for all tracker work (standard complexity). Adds tracker_items (version, deleted_at, key_number), tracker_vocabularies (kind, position), tracker_item_labels, tracker_item_assignees, tracker_events and workspaces.tracker_key_counter; board tables must stay untouched. Kysely interfaces hand-added to server/src/db/types.ts.

nodes.label: Tracker Key Utilities
nodes.rationale: server/src/core/tracker-key.ts: derivePrefix (workspace initials → key prefix, e.g. 'Camel'→'CA'), formatKey, parseKeyFromUrl (inverse, supports stale-prefix redirect). derivePrefix must stay in parity with client/src/lib/workspaceSwitcher.ts workspaceInitials().

nodes.label: Tracker Vocabulary API
nodes.rationale: List/create endpoints in server/src/routes/tracker-vocabularies.ts over the unified vocabulary table (Option A); case-insensitive duplicate-name rejection (400/409), fractional position on create, auto pastel colour. No delete/rename endpoints.

nodes.label: Tracker Vocabulary Seed
nodes.rationale: Idempotent (ON CONFLICT / WHERE NOT EXISTS) retroactive seed so pre-tracker workspaces get default status (Backlog/Todo/In Progress/Done/Canceled), priority (High/Medium/Low) and label (Feature/Bug/Maintain) vocabulary without duplication on re-run.

nodes.label: Tracker Client API Layer
nodes.rationale: Adds TrackerItem/TrackerVocabulary types to client/src/types.ts and api.ts methods createTrackerItem, listTrackerItems, updateTrackerItem (PATCH with version), getTrackerItem, deleteTrackerItem, getTrackerChangelog, listTrackerVocabularies, createTrackerVocabulary.

nodes.label: Tracker Changelog
nodes.rationale: GET /tracker/items/:key/events mirrors server/src/routes/activity.ts; returns per-item changelog events read from tracker_events.

nodes.label: Tracker Items API
nodes.rationale: Core API surface (deep complexity): create with atomic key, ILIKE list search, detail with stale-prefix redirect metadata (canonicalKey/redirectFrom), PATCH with version/409, soft delete (deleted_at, key never reused), multi-assignee, per-item changelog. Mirrors cards version/409 and assignee patterns; every mutation calls recordTrackerActivity; member role can CRUD.

nodes.label: Tracker Realtime SSE Events
nodes.rationale: Extends the BoardEvent union in server/src/realtime.ts with tracker.* event types (tracker.created, tracker.updated, tracker.deleted, tracker.vocabulary.created) published via publishEvent from item and vocabulary routes; must not change card event type behavior.

nodes.label: subscribeTrackerEvents (BoardContext SSE Registry)
nodes.rationale: BoardContext registry added in T7 that dispatches tracker SSE events to subscribers; extended in T8 to handle tracker.updated/tracker.deleted for the detail page.

nodes.label: Tracker Detail Page (TrackerDetailPage)
nodes.rationale: /tracker/:key page with edit form, per-item changelog (TrackerChangelog), stale-prefix redirect to canonical key, 409 conflict toast UX mirroring cards, and live SSE updates via BoardContext dispatch (tracker.updated applies live, tracker.deleted removes from list).

nodes.label: Tracker List Page (TrackerPage)
nodes.rationale: /tracker page built from TrackerPage + TrackerRow + TrackerSection + TrackerCreateModal + trackerUtils: status-grouped dense Linear-style rows, sections ordered by vocabulary position, in-memory search and collapse (no URL state/localStorage), global + opens create modal, live vocab sections via tracker SSE. Nav entry between Board and Inbox.

nodes.label: Tracker Entity
nodes.rationale: New work-item tracking feature parallel to the kanban board: DB schema, vocabulary, items CRUD/search/assignees/changelog, realtime SSE, client API layer, list and detail pages.

nodes.label: Tracker Entity Plan Closeout
nodes.rationale: Closeout record: all phases DONE, all reviewable tasks REVIEW_PASS (started 2026-08-03, closed 2026-08-04, baseline 7c4e7a1a..final ed3282f5). Records per-task done SHAs, corrections (T7, T8) and non-blocking carried-forward review observations.

nodes.label: Tracker Entity Execution Plan
nodes.rationale: Approved master plan (GitHub issue #87, spec docs/pocket/spec/2026-08-03-tracker-entity/tracker-entity.md) with 8 TDD tasks in order T1→T2→T3→T4→T5/T6(parallel)→T7→T8, Vitest test framework, RUN_INTEGRATION=1 gating for server integration tests, and plan-validation fixes applied after external review (grade C+ → execution-ready).

nodes.label: Atomic Tracker Key Counter
nodes.rationale: Keys like CA-42 are allocated from a per-workspace atomic counter (workspaces.tracker_key_counter) so concurrent creates get unique keys and key numbers are never reused, even after soft delete.

nodes.label: Version-based Optimistic Locking (409)
nodes.rationale: PATCH requires a version; a stale version returns 409 version_conflict so concurrent edits surface a conflict UX instead of silently overwriting — mirrors the cards pattern.

nodes.label: Tracker–Board Separation Constraint
nodes.rationale: Architecture rule: do NOT touch Board/cards/columns or card_events/recordActivity; tracker mutations must write only to tracker_events via recordTrackerActivity(). Keeps tracker activity data fully independent from the kanban board.

nodes.label: Camel Kanban Board
nodes.rationale: Product positioning: a calm, real-time kanban board for small and growing teams — with work-in-progress limits, live flow metrics, and built-in AI that researches and writes for you; GitHub issues integration; free to self-host. Visual design intent: Work Sans typography, navy theme color #172a3e, logo.png for social sharing.

nodes.label: Text-to-Lottie
nodes.rationale: Open-source harness for generating production-ready Lottie animations with claude code/codex or any coding agent supporting skills. Design intent behind the prompt guide: ground the model with concrete assets (SVGs, real-world data, screenshots) because results are significantly better on concrete assets; use motion design terminology (ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out); think like a camera operator (pushes, pans, zooms, rig-like motion simulated via group transforms); explicitly request the controls you need (outputs usually only expose a background color control by default); specify FPS and duration when a specific frame rate or length matters.

nodes.label: Lottie Loading & Success Animations

nodes.label: Prompt Guide Principles
nodes.rationale: Five prompting principles: ground the model with concrete assets, use motion design terminology, think like a camera operator, request the controls you need, and specify FPS/duration. These exist because grounding on concrete assets and using motion language measurably improves output quality.
